chapter: Moving to New Orleans and country bands
title: Moving to New Orleans after the 1915 storm
summary: He moved up the day after the 1915 storm after staying with an aunt; Sam was already in the city.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was wondering about, maybe you told when I was running the machine and didn't hear, when you moved up from the country, how old were you? When did you move to New Orleans?
I moved the day after that 1915 storm. I don't blame you.
Had Sam in the other state or was Sam up here playing already?
Well, no Sam was up here.

Yeah. Then I had been coming up here. I had an auntie waking up on St. Charles Street, right St. Charles and Louisiana Avenue for a man from down the country down there. Well, I stayed up there with her a while before the storm. You know what I mean? I'd come and go, come and go. But I was in the country when that storm came up. And I was laying down in the bed and that 1915 storm came up. And when I seen that house on joint like that, I said, it's time for me to go. Fell apart up the rafters, huh? Yes. I mean, come on party. So I moved up. Went over to somebody else's house. And the Mississippi River man was boiling. Like he was angry.
That was down, way down below Violet. Is it farther than Pointe?
Oh man, that's 30 miles down. 30 miles away. That's the place at the place called Belay. Belay. Same as these Fools called. Old man John Diamond's place.
